text: In render/json.go, `JSON.Render` calls `WriteJSON(w, r.Data)`; if that returns a non-nil error it does not return it — it `panic(err)`s (the named return `err` is left as the panic value, so the error surfaces as a panic, which gin's Recovery middleware turns into a 500). Note this differs from the other renderers (IndentedJSON, SecureJSON, etc.), which return the error.
SetMode("") with no "test.v" flag set: value is set to DebugMode ("debug"), so ginMode = debugCode and modeName = "debug".
Mode() returns the package-level `modeName` string (the current mode name: "debug", "release" or "test"), set by SetMode.
#1 (errors.go): ETA ~10 min. #4 (response_writer.go): ETA ~5 min — the missing `return` in WriteHeader is identified and a subagent is applying/verifying the fix now.

#1 (errors.go): ETA ~8 min. #4 (response_writer.go): ETA ~3 min (fix identified, being verified). #8 (tree.go, TestRouteParamsNotEmpty): ETA ~12 min. #11 (tree.go, TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePathWithMultipleChildrenAndWildcard): ETA ~12 min.

#4 (response_writer.go): DONE. Added the missing `return` after the "Headers were already written" warning in `responseWriter.WriteHeader`, so the status code is no longer overwritten once headers are written. Verified: full suite `go test ./...` passes, and a temporary test (WriteHeader(200) → WriteHeaderNow() → WriteHeader(500) → Status()==200) passes with the fix and fails without it.

defaultHandleRecovery(c *Context, err any) calls `c.AbortWithStatus(http.StatusInternalServerError)` — it aborts the request and sets the response status to 500 (the recovered panic value is ignored).
defaultValidator.lazyinit() calls validator.New() and then v.validate.SetTagName("binding") — so the tag name is "binding".
defaultValidator.ValidateStruct(nil) returns nil immediately (it checks `if obj == nil { return nil }` before doing anything else).

#1 (errors.go): DONE — Unwrap now has a value receiver, so gin.Error values satisfy errors.Is/As/Unwrap; TestErrorUnwrap passes. #4 (response_writer.go): DONE — missing `return` added in WriteHeader. #8 (tree.go, TestRouteParamsNotEmpty): ETA ~10 min. #11 (tree.go, TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePathWithMultipleChildrenAndWildcard): ETA ~10 min. #15 (context.go, TestContextNegotiationFormat2): ETA ~8 min. #18 (context.go, TestContextRenderAndEscapeAttachment): ETA ~6 min. Fixes for #15 and #18 are being applied and verified now.
When the field's `time_format` tag is empty, setTimeField falls back to `timeFormat = time.RFC3339` (i.e. "2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00"), and parses with time.ParseInLocation(timeFormat, val, l).

SecureJSON.Render writes r.Prefix before the marshaled JSON only when the marshaled bytes are a JSON array — i.e. when jsonBytes has prefix "[" and suffix "]". Otherwise it writes only the JSON bytes.

#18 (context.go, TestContextRenderAndEscapeAttachment): DONE. FileAttachment's ASCII branch now uses a new `escapeQuotes` helper (added in utils.go, same replacer net/http uses) so quotes/backslashes in the filename are escaped. Verified: existing attachment tests pass, and a temporary test asserting `attachment; filename="<escapeQuotes(name)>"` passes.

#15 (context.go, TestContextNegotiationFormat2): DONE. NegotiateFormat indexed `offer[i]` up to len(accepted), so an offer shorter than the accepted type (e.g. offer "text" with Accept "text/html") panicked with index out of range. Loop is now bounded by both lengths (`i < len(accepted) && i < len(offer)`), so such cases return "" instead of panicking; all existing negotiation tests still pass and the previously-panicking probe cases now return "" with all other results unchanged.
